findings.title: Upsampling decision ignores the query actually executed
findings.body: _get_event_stats decides upsampling from the closed-over dataset and request.GET query, not from scoped_dataset or the query argument it is about to run. Dashboard discover-split rewrites that argument (for example to event.type:transaction or !event.type:transaction) and sometimes switches the dataset, but the count() -> upsampled_count() rewrite still follows the original request. Transaction or mixed queries can then sum sample_weight (missing or meaningless on those events), and error-only split queries can skip upsampling even when every project is allowlisted. Counts are wrong or the Snuba query fails.

findings.title: errors dataset rewrites count() to an undefined function
findings.body: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True for the errors dataset, and the stats endpoint then replaces count() with upsampled_count(). That function is only registered on the discover dataset function converter. Errors-dataset timeseries requests for allowlisted projects will fail column/function resolution instead of returning an upsampled count.

findings.title: Upsampled count sums sample_weight, but tests only set sample_rate
findings.body: upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). The new store_event hook writes contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate into sample_rate (0.1 for a 10x sample) after manager.get_data(), and never sets sample_weight to 1/sample_rate. If weight was already derived, this mutation is too late; if Snuba reads sample_weight, the aggregate stays ~1 (or 0 if the column is null) while the new stats test expects 10. toInt64 also truncates fractional weights, so partial samples under-count even when the column is populated.

findings.title: Eligibility cache key uses salted hash()
findings.body: The cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so each worker writes and reads a different key, and invalidate_upsampling_cache cannot delete keys other workers stored. The 60s cache does not dedupe option lookups across the fleet, and a hash collision could reuse another project set's allowlist decision. Nothing in this change calls the invalidator when the allowlist option changes, so a stable key would still be stale for up to 60s.

findings.title: Error-query check is a substring match
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query treats any query whose lowercased text contains "event.type:error" as error-only. That matches the negation !event.type:error, event.type:error.unhandled-style tokens, and the same text inside a quoted string or OR branch that also selects transactions. Discover queries that are not purely errors then get count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight), which mis-counts or errors on events that do not have that column.
